mainText:
The election has delivered no clear winner, with special votes now set to decide who governs New Zealand.

New Zealand.

Election night ended in deadlock. On-the-night counting pointed to a one-seat majority for the current coalition, but Labour's Chris Hipkins has not conceded, and Christopher Luxon himself called the result too close to call. New Zealand is now under caretaker government conventions while counting continues. The Opportunity Party looks set to enter Parliament for the first time, with close to six percent of the party vote and seven MPs, the first party to enter under MMP from outside Parliament. Several senior National MPs lost their seats, including Chris Bishop, who says he's unlikely to return, trailing Labour's Ginny Andersen by eight hundred and eighty nine votes in Hutt South. Mahesh Muralidhar becomes National's first Indian electorate MP, retaking Tāmaki from ACT. Five electorates remain on a knife edge, with as few as one hundred and thirty nine votes separating candidates in the closest race. Special votes will not be finalised for about two weeks, and coalition talks will follow once they are.

Severe thunderstorms swept across large parts of the North Island on election day before clearing. Fireworks are being blamed for an extensive fire that damaged public toilets and changing rooms in Hamilton, with police appealing for information about a group seen firing fireworks at each other.

In Western Bay of Plenty, Tauranga-area councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision has triggered a byelection. He says the decision was, in his words, absolutely the right one despite the cost.

Police in Tauranga are reviewing two convoys totalling two hundred vehicles that drove through Tauranga and Mount Maunganui last weekend during Rugby League World Cup celebrations, with speakers blaring and people hanging from windows.

Wall Street's heavy tech sell-off has so far left New Zealand shares relatively steady, though analysts expect the buoyant New Zealand stock exchange to come under pressure after it hit a record high last week.

World.

A gunman in military fatigues opened fire in Krakow's main square, killing at least six people. Polish authorities are investigating the attack, Poland's second largest city.

Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry says at least twenty five people were killed and thirty wounded in air strikes on a village near the capital Sanaa, mostly women and children. Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis, has not commented.

Donald Trump has told reporters he wants UFC boss Dana White to become his new White House press secretary, with mixed martial arts fighters as assistants. The White House has not confirmed whether the offer was serious.

Paraguay's ousted president Santiago Pena has been charged following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions of people unable to access their accounts. He was impeached over the banking crisis and appeared before prosecutors at the weekend.

Technology.

Global stock markets fell sharply before paring losses, as fears over a slowdown in artificial intelligence spending spread from the United States through Asia and Europe. Shares in AI-linked companies have since climbed back after trillions were wiped from market values, with investors reacting to expectations of tougher scrutiny of data centre construction.

Binance says the record six point three billion US dollar hack of its exchange used fake job interviews, contacting an engineer through a legitimate job-hunting platform before inviting him to bogus interviews with fake company staff. North Korea denies involvement, despite United States agencies and cyber analysts blaming Pyongyang.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks beat Scotland forty three to twenty one at Murrayfield, scoreless in the second half after two early yellow cards. Beauden Barrett scored twice. The match followed the death of the team's security chief, Logan Cadwallader, at their Edinburgh hotel during the week, with Barrett saying the win was dedicated to him.

Rugby League World Cup. The Kiwis beat Tonga to reach their first final since twenty thirteen, with Kalyn Ponga starring in his return from a broken arm. They face either the Kangaroos or Samoa next Sunday night at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane. The Kiwi Ferns beat Fetu Samoa thirty two to nil to reach their final, Stacey Waka scoring a hat trick.

Football. Auckland FC and the Wellington Phoenix drew nil all in their first derby of the season, leaving the Phoenix unbeaten against their rivals but still without a win over them.

Cricket. The Black Caps lost the second one day international to India in Wellington, with the Duckworth Lewis Stanley method coming into play after rain.

Formula One. Liam Lawson goes into this weekend's race still without clarity on his twenty twenty seven seat.

Basketball. The New Zealand Breakers lost a fifth straight National Basketball League match, an undermanned side staying bottom of the standings.

Coming up. Special votes continue to be counted over the next two weeks, with coalition talks to follow. The Kiwis play the World Cup final next Sunday night in Brisbane. The All Blacks play Wales in Cardiff this coming weekend.

End of flash.
